easy.question: Who died in these verses?
answers: Sarah
Rebekah
Rachel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Sarah died.”

easy.question: How old was Sarah when she died?
answers: 120 years old
127 years old
137 years old
easy.explanation: The verse counts one hundred years, twenty years, and seven years—127 years in all.

easy.question: What did Abraham do after Sarah died?
answers: He went to war
He built a city
He mourned for her and wept
easy.explanation: Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and weep for her.

medium.question: What did Abraham do after Sarah died, according to the phrase “Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her”?
answers: He mourned and wept
He buried her immediately
He celebrated
medium.explanation: The verse directly says that Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and weep for her.

medium.question: What is the relationship between Sarah’s death and Abraham’s actions?
answers: Because Sarah died, Abraham came to mourn and weep
Because Sarah died, Abraham began a journey
Because Sarah died, Abraham celebrated
medium.explanation: The verse first describes Sarah’s death and then says that Abraham came to mourn and weep.

medium.question: Where did Sarah die?

In Kirjatharba, which is Hebron in Canaan
In Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The verse says that Sarah died in Kirjatharba, which is Hebron in the land of Canaan.

Sarah lived for only two years
Sarah lived in only two countries

“The same is Hebron”
“Abraham came”

answers: Sarah died, Abraham came, and he mourned and wept
Abraham wept, Sarah died, and then he came
Abraham came, Sarah died, and then he wept
challenge.explanation: The verses first describe Sarah’s death, then Abraham’s arrival, followed by his mourning and weeping.

answers: The separate numbers together describe all her years

Sarah lived in only two countries

Abraham wept, Sarah died, and then he came
Abraham came, Sarah died, and then he wept
questions.explanation: The verses first describe Sarah’s death, then Abraham’s arrival, followed by his mourning and weeping.

easy.question: What did Abraham do after rising from before his dead?
answers: He went home
He spoke to the sons of Heth
He bought a field
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abraham rose from before his dead and then spoke to the sons of Heth.

easy.question: To whom did Abraham speak?
answers: The sons of Heth
Isaac
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And spake unto the sons of Heth.”

easy.question: What did Abraham ask the sons of Heth for?
answers: A flock of sheep
A house
A burial place of his own
easy.explanation: Abraham asked for a permanent place where he could bury his dead.

medium.question: Why did Abraham describe himself as “a stranger and a sojourner”?
answers: To say that he was their king
To explain that he lived among them but owned no burial property there
To ask them to leave the land
medium.explanation: Abraham lived among the Hittites, but he had no property of his own for a burial place.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: Abraham rose, spoke to the sons of Heth, and asked for a burial place
Abraham buried the dead, rose, and then spoke
The sons of Heth offered a place, and then Abraham rose
medium.explanation: Abraham first rose, then addressed the sons of Heth, and finally requested a burial place.

medium.question: What does the phrase “a possession of a buryingplace” mean in context?
answers: A special garment for mourners
A burial ceremony
A permanent burial place belonging to someone
medium.explanation: The phrase describes property set aside as a permanent place for burial.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “a stranger and a sojourner” about Abraham’s situation?
answers: He lived there but did not own the land or property there
He did not intend to remain in the land
He belonged to the family of the sons of Heth
challenge.explanation: The phrase combines living in a place with not being its native owner.

challenge.question: How does Abraham’s description as “a stranger and a sojourner” relate to his request?
answers: He asks the sons of Heth to sell him the whole land
He explains why he needs their permission to obtain a burial place
He announces that he will leave immediately
challenge.explanation: Because he lived among them without owning property, Abraham appealed to them for a burial place.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “bury my dead out of my sight”?
answers: Abraham is speaking about someone who died long ago
Abraham wants to bury someone he does not know
Abraham wants to remove his dead from where he is and bury him in a suitable place
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that Abraham wants his dead removed from before him and buried elsewhere.

He belonged to the family of the sons of Heth
questions.explanation: The phrase combines living in a place with not being its native owner.

answers: He asks the sons of Heth to sell him the whole land

He announces that he will leave immediately
questions.explanation: Because he lived among them without owning property, Abraham appealed to them for a burial place.

answers: Abraham is speaking about someone who died long ago

Abraham wants to remove his dead from where he is and bury him in a suitable place
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that Abraham wants his dead removed from before him and buried elsewhere.

paragraphs.title: The Sons of Heth Honor Abraham

easy.question: Who answered Abraham in these verses?
answers: The sons of Heth
The Israelites
The Egyptians
easy.explanation: The verse says that the children of Heth answered Abraham.

easy.question: How did the sons of Heth address Abraham?
answers: Great king
My lord
My father
easy.explanation: They began by saying, “Hear us, my lord.”

easy.question: What did the sons of Heth offer Abraham?
answers: To leave the land
To buy him a house
To bury his dead in one of their tombs
easy.explanation: They told him to bury his dead in the choice of their sepulchres.

medium.question: Why did the sons of Heth agree to let Abraham bury his dead in their sepulchres?
answers: Because they honored him as a mighty prince among them
Because he was their king
Because he asked them to leave
medium.explanation: They said, “Thou art a mighty prince among us,” and therefore offered him their best burial places.

medium.question: What does “the choice of our sepulchres” mean?
answers: The most distant tombs
The best or finest tombs
The smallest tombs
medium.explanation: “Choice” refers to the finest or most desirable burial places.

medium.question: What was the order of events in these verses?
answers: The sons of Heth buried the dead and then answered Abraham
Abraham bought a tomb and then addressed the sons of Heth
The sons of Heth answered Abraham and then offered him a tomb
medium.explanation: They first answered Abraham, and in their answer offered him one of their sepulchres.

challenge.question: What does “none of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre” mean?
answers: No one will prevent you from choosing a tomb and burying your dead
No one will see you
No one will know the dead person
challenge.explanation: They assure Abraham that none of them will stop him from choosing a burial place.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “among us” in “thou art a mighty prince among us”?
answers: Abraham was outside their land
Abraham lived among them and in their community
Abraham ruled the whole world
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that Abraham was present within the community of the sons of Heth.

challenge.question: What does the title “a mighty prince” express?
answers: That Abraham was a temple priest
That he was king over the sons of Heth
That they regarded him as a person of special status and honor
challenge.explanation: The title is an expression of respect and explains their generous offer.

questions.question: What does “none of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre” mean?
answers: No one will prevent you from choosing a tomb and burying your dead
No one will see you
No one will know the dead person
questions.explanation: They assure Abraham that none of them will stop him from choosing a burial place.

questions.question: What can be understood from “among us” in “thou art a mighty prince among us”?
answers: Abraham was outside their land
Abraham lived among them and in their community
Abraham ruled the whole world
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that Abraham was present within the community of the sons of Heth.

questions.question: What does the title “a mighty prince” express?
answers: That Abraham was a temple priest
That he was king over the sons of Heth
That they regarded him as a person of special status and honor
questions.explanation: The title is an expression of respect and explains their generous offer.

paragraphs.title: The Request for the Cave of Machpelah

easy.question: Who rose and bowed to the people of the land?
answers: Abraham
Ephron
The sons of Heth
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land.

easy.question: Whom did Abraham ask them to approach for him?
answers: The sons of Heth
Ephron son of Zohar
Isaac
easy.explanation: Abraham asked them to “intreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar.”

easy.question: Why did Abraham ask for the cave of Machpelah?
answers: To live in it
To work the land
To make it a burial possession
easy.explanation: He wanted the cave as a possession for a burial place.

medium.question: Why did Abraham ask the sons of Heth to approach Ephron?
answers: So they could ask Ephron to sell him the cave
So they could build him a house
So they could take the cave for themselves
medium.explanation: Abraham asked them to speak to Ephron, the owner of the cave, so that he could purchase it.

medium.question: What does “intreat for me to Ephron” mean in context?
answers: Strike him
Approach him and ask him on my behalf
Run away from him
medium.explanation: Abraham asks them to speak with Ephron and make the request for him.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: Abraham bought the field and then bowed
The sons of Heth buried the dead and then Abraham spoke
Abraham bowed, spoke to the sons of Heth, and asked to buy the cave
medium.explanation: Abraham first bowed, then spoke to the sons of Heth, and finally requested the cave for its full value.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “for as much money as it is worth” show about Abraham’s request?
answers: He intended to pay the full price
He wanted the cave for free
He intended to pay only part of the price
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that Abraham was prepared to pay the complete and fair value.

challenge.question: Which best describes the property Abraham requested?
answers: Ephron’s entire field
A particular cave at the end of the field
A house inside the city
challenge.explanation: Abraham requested the cave of Machpelah, which was at the end of Ephron’s field.

challenge.question: What combination of respect and practical action appears in Abraham’s words?
answers: He took the cave without permission
He asked only for temporary use of the cave
He honored the people of the land and asked to purchase the cave
challenge.explanation: Abraham bowed respectfully but also proposed a clear purchase for the full price.

questions.question: What does the phrase “for as much money as it is worth” show about Abraham’s request?
answers: He intended to pay the full price
He wanted the cave for free
He intended to pay only part of the price
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that Abraham was prepared to pay the complete and fair value.

questions.question: Which best describes the property Abraham requested?
answers: Ephron’s entire field
A particular cave at the end of the field
A house inside the city
questions.explanation: Abraham requested the cave of Machpelah, which was at the end of Ephron’s field.

questions.question: What combination of respect and practical action appears in Abraham’s words?
answers: He took the cave without permission
He asked only for temporary use of the cave
He honored the people of the land and asked to purchase the cave
questions.explanation: Abraham bowed respectfully but also proposed a clear purchase for the full price.

paragraphs.title: Ephron Offers the Field and the Cave

easy.question: Who answered Abraham in these verses?
answers: Ephron
The sons of Heth
The people of the land
easy.explanation: Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham.

easy.question: What did Ephron offer Abraham?
answers: Only the field
The field and the cave
Only the cave
easy.explanation: Ephron said that he would give Abraham both the field and the cave in it.

easy.question: What did Abraham do after Ephron spoke?
answers: He left the place
He bought the city
He bowed before the people of the land
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abraham bowed before the people of the land.

medium.question: Why is Ephron said to have spoken “in the audience of the children of Heth”?
answers: So that many witnesses would know his words
So Abraham could not hear him
So he could invite them to a feast
medium.explanation: Ephron spoke publicly so that the sons of Heth and those at the city gate could hear his offer.

medium.question: What does “hear me” mean in Ephron’s words, “Nay, my lord, hear me”?
answers: Go away
Listen to me
Pay me
medium.explanation: Ephron is asking Abraham to listen to what he is saying.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Abraham bowed, and then Ephron offered the field and cave
Ephron offered the field and cave, and then Abraham bowed
The sons of Heth buried the dead, and then Ephron spoke
medium.explanation: Ephron first made his offer, and afterward Abraham bowed before the people of the land.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Ephron’s words “in the presence of the sons of my people”?
answers: The offer was made publicly and before witnesses
He spoke only with his family
He hid the offer from Abraham
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that Ephron’s people saw and heard the offer and could serve as witnesses.

challenge.question: What did Abraham’s bowing show about his response to Ephron?
answers: He was angry with Ephron
He expressed respect and appreciation
He gave up on burying his dead
challenge.explanation: Bowing before the people of the land expressed respect and appreciation.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that Ephron offered Abraham more than was needed for the burial?
answers: He sat among the sons of Heth
He spoke at the city gate
He mentioned both the field and the cave
challenge.explanation: The cave was needed for burial, but Ephron explicitly mentioned the surrounding field as well.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Ephron’s words “in the presence of the sons of my people”?
answers: The offer was made publicly and before witnesses
He spoke only with his family
He hid the offer from Abraham
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that Ephron’s people saw and heard the offer and could serve as witnesses.

questions.question: What did Abraham’s bowing show about his response to Ephron?
answers: He was angry with Ephron
He expressed respect and appreciation
He gave up on burying his dead
questions.explanation: Bowing before the people of the land expressed respect and appreciation.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that Ephron offered Abraham more than was needed for the burial?
answers: He sat among the sons of Heth
He spoke at the city gate
He mentioned both the field and the cave
questions.explanation: The cave was needed for burial, but Ephron explicitly mentioned the surrounding field as well.

easy.question: What did Abraham ask Ephron to do?
answers: Sell him the field for money
Give him the field as a gift
Bury his dead in another field
easy.explanation: Abraham offered to pay for the field so that he could bury his dead there.

easy.question: How much did Ephron say the land was worth?
answers: Two hundred shekels of silver
Four hundred shekels of silver
Five hundred shekels of silver
easy.explanation: Ephron said that the land was worth four hundred shekels of silver.

easy.question: What did Abraham do after hearing Ephron’s words?
answers: He left the place
He asked for a discount
He weighed the silver to Ephron
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abraham weighed out the silver to Ephron.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Abraham offered money, Ephron named the price, and Abraham weighed the money
Ephron weighed the money, Abraham buried his dead, and then the price was set
Abraham asked for a gift, Ephron refused, and Abraham left
medium.explanation: Abraham first offered to pay, Ephron named the price, and Abraham then paid it.

medium.question: What does “hearken unto me” mean in “My lord, hearken unto me”?
answers: Look at me
Listen to me
Forgive me
medium.explanation: Ephron asks Abraham to listen to his statement about the value of the land.

medium.question: Why is it emphasized that Abraham spoke before the people of the land and Ephron before the sons of Heth?
answers: To show that no one heard the transaction
To emphasize that they spoke secretly
So that the agreement and price would be known to witnesses
medium.explanation: Their public statements show that the negotiation and payment took place openly and before witnesses.

challenge.question: What does Ephron’s phrase “what is that betwixt me and thee?” mean?
answers: He presents the amount as a small matter between them
He says he does not know the field’s price
He cancels the possibility of selling the field
challenge.explanation: Ephron names the price but rhetorically describes the amount as insignificant between them.

challenge.question: What does “current money with the merchant” show about the silver Abraham paid?
answers: It was old and no longer used
It was accepted currency for trade
It was immediately passed to another merchant
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes silver of recognized and reliable value in commerce.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Abraham weighing the full amount Ephron named before the sons of Heth?
answers: Abraham wanted to delay the purchase
Abraham did not understand the price
Abraham accepted the price and completed the transaction clearly
challenge.explanation: Abraham did not argue over the price; he publicly weighed the four hundred shekels and completed the purchase.

questions.question: What does Ephron’s phrase “what is that betwixt me and thee?” mean?
answers: He presents the amount as a small matter between them
He says he does not know the field’s price
He cancels the possibility of selling the field
questions.explanation: Ephron names the price but rhetorically describes the amount as insignificant between them.

questions.question: What does “current money with the merchant” show about the silver Abraham paid?
answers: It was old and no longer used
It was accepted currency for trade
It was immediately passed to another merchant
questions.explanation: The phrase describes silver of recognized and reliable value in commerce.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Abraham weighing the full amount Ephron named before the sons of Heth?
answers: Abraham wanted to delay the purchase
Abraham did not understand the price
Abraham accepted the price and completed the transaction clearly
questions.explanation: Abraham did not argue over the price; he publicly weighed the four hundred shekels and completed the purchase.

paragraphs.title: The Purchase of the Field and Sarah’s Burial

easy.question: What did Abraham buy from Ephron?
answers: A field, a cave, and the trees in it
A house in the city
A flock of sheep
easy.explanation: The verses describe the field, the cave in it, and all the trees within its borders.

easy.question: Whom did Abraham bury in the cave of Machpelah?
answers: Rebekah
Sarah his wife
Rachel
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Abraham buried Sarah his wife.

easy.question: In what region was the cave of Machpelah located?
answers: Egypt
Philistia
The land of Canaan
easy.explanation: The cave was in Hebron, in the land of Canaan.

medium.question: What does “in the presence of the children of Heth” mean in connection with the purchase?
answers: The purchase was secret and without witnesses
The purchase took place in the presence of the sons of Heth
It took place before Sarah’s family only
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the purchase was made openly before the sons of Heth.

medium.question: What happened after the field and cave became Abraham’s?
answers: Abraham buried Sarah
Ephron buried Sarah
The sons of Heth sold another field
medium.explanation: After the purchase, Abraham buried Sarah in the cave.

medium.question: What does “for a possession of a buryingplace” mean in this passage?
answers: A burial place belonging to Abraham
A market for selling tombs
A cave that no one could enter
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the field and cave became Abraham’s permanent property for burial.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the purchase being made before “all that went in at the gate of his city”?
answers: The transaction was public and known to the city’s residents
Only Ephron knew about it
The field was outside every settlement
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the people present at the city gate, showing that the purchase was public.

challenge.question: What property was included in the purchase?
answers: The cave alone
The field, the cave, and all the trees within its borders
The whole city of Hebron
challenge.explanation: The verse lists the field, the cave, and all the trees within the field’s boundaries.

challenge.question: What is the significance of the order—first the property was made sure to Abraham, and afterward he buried Sarah?
answers: Abraham buried Sarah before owning the place
The burial took place after ownership of the burial place was established
The burial caused the sons of Heth to sell the field
challenge.explanation: The order emphasizes that the purchase and recognition of ownership came before Sarah’s burial.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the purchase being made before “all that went in at the gate of his city”?
answers: The transaction was public and known to the city’s residents
Only Ephron knew about it
The field was outside every settlement
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the people present at the city gate, showing that the purchase was public.

questions.question: What property was included in the purchase?
answers: The cave alone
The field, the cave, and all the trees within its borders
The whole city of Hebron
questions.explanation: The verse lists the field, the cave, and all the trees within the field’s boundaries.

questions.question: What is the significance of the order—first the property was made sure to Abraham, and afterward he buried Sarah?
answers: Abraham buried Sarah before owning the place
The burial took place after ownership of the burial place was established
The burial caused the sons of Heth to sell the field
questions.explanation: The order emphasizes that the purchase and recognition of ownership came before Sarah’s burial.
